title: Polars: columnar data engineering
summary: A complete route through typed tables, expression semantics, temporal correctness, lazy execution, Arrow interoperability, measured performance and validated data publication.

lessons.title: Rows, columns, schemas and expressions
lessons.outcome: Construct and verify a typed table with a stated row grain.
lessons.lab: Add a revenue expression to a three-row orders table and confirm that it keeps one row per order and a total of 30, then filter to an empty frame and check that its Int64 and String schema survives.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Revenue is [10, 8, 12], total 30; input shape remains 3 by 3 and output shape is 3 by 4. Worked case 2: The empty frame has 0 rows and the original Int64/String schema; selecting label,id produces that order.

lessons.title: Expression contexts and explicit dependencies
lessons.outcome: Build a transformation whose dependency stages are explicit.
lessons.lab: Compare one with_columns call that reads the original x with two staged calls that read the updated x, then build a when/then recognized amount and observe the ColumnNotFoundError for a missing column.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The same-call multiplication is [10, 20, 30]; the staged multiplication is [20, 30, 40]. Worked case 2: Recognized amounts are [5, 0, 11]; selecting a missing column is rejected.

lessons.title: Types, parsing failures and exact numeric values
lessons.outcome: Implement a parsing policy that preserves rejected evidence.
lessons.lab: Parse text quantities with a non-strict cast, separate malformed tokens from missing ones, watch a strict cast reject the bad token, and check Decimal totals and Int8 narrowing.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Record 2 is malformed, record 3 is missing, and parsed units are [2, null, null, 4]. Worked case 2: Decimal total is 0.30; the Int8 conversion gives [127, null].

lessons.title: Null, NaN and three-valued logic
lessons.outcome: Explain how missingness changes a specific calculation.
lessons.lab: Count null and NaN separately in a float column, apply an explicit fill policy for each, and trace which rows a filter keeps when the Boolean predicate is null.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: One null and one NaN are identified; the chosen final values are [1, 0, 0, 4]. Worked case 2: The default filter retains id 1; an explicit unknown-is-true policy retains ids 1 and 3.

lessons.title: Aggregation grain and weighted quantities
lessons.outcome: Build an aggregate whose numerator, denominator and weighting unit are explicit.
lessons.lab: Pool successes and trials per group instead of averaging row rates, and summarize groups whose values are partly or wholly missing without losing their row and observation counts.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The pooled rates are \(A=0.1\) and \(B=0.5\); the equal-row average for \(A\) is approximately \(0.545\). Worked case 2: Group A has 2 rows, 1 observed value and mean 2; group B has 1 row, 0 observed values and null mean.

lessons.title: Joins, cardinality and reconciliation
lessons.outcome: Enrich a fact table while proving its grain and totals remain valid.
lessons.lab: Enrich orders with a validated many-to-one join, reproduce the fanout a duplicated dimension key causes, and audit membership with semi and anti joins under an explicit null-key policy.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Correct rows 3/total 21; duplicate dimension gives 5 rows/total 33; m:1 validation rejects it. Worked case 2: Default matching retains id 1; anti retains ids 2 and 3; explicit null matching also retains id 3.

lessons.title: Time zones, elapsed time and interval boundaries
lessons.outcome: Define time semantics before aggregating a dataset.
lessons.lab: Convert UTC timestamps across a daylight-saving change and compare displayed hours with elapsed seconds, then split events into half-open periods so a boundary event is counted once.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Displayed hours are [1, 3], while elapsed time is 3,600 seconds. Worked case 2: The first period totals 5, the next totals 5, and all three rows occur exactly once.

lessons.title: Reshaping while preserving identity
lessons.outcome: Reshape a repeated-measurement dataset with a checked compound key.
lessons.lab: Unpivot a paired before/after table and pivot it back to the identical frame, then show that duplicate id-period cells are rejected until an aggregation policy is chosen.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The long table has four rows and the reconstructed wide table equals its source. Worked case 2: Duplicate cell frequency is 2; an explicit sum is 10; an unspecified aggregation fails.

lessons.title: Ordered windows and row-preserving statistics
lessons.outcome: Create row-preserving historical features with explicit ordering.
lessons.lab: Sort events by customer and time before computing running and previous values with over, then center values on a group mean while keeping every input row.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Customer A running totals are [2, 7, 11], customer B has 7, and first predecessors are null. Worked case 2: Window output has three rows; grouped means have two rows.

lessons.title: Lazy plans and optimizer reasoning
lessons.outcome: Explain a lazy query in terms of its requested result and observable execution plan.
lessons.lab: Write a small Parquet file, build a lazy scan with a filter and projection, read its optimized plan, and show that filtering before or after a group mean changes the result.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Ids [2, 3] have doubled values [24, 40], and the result schema contains exactly two fields. Worked case 2: Filtering group means retains only B; filtering values first retains A and B.

lessons.title: Files, schema boundaries and columnar artifacts
lessons.outcome: Publish a small typed artifact with independently checked readback.
lessons.lab: Combine two Parquet parts through scan_parquet and sink_parquet, verify the readback values and schema, and quarantine a malformed CSV amount instead of coercing it.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The combined artifact contains ids [1, 2, 3] with total value 10.5. Worked case 2: Id 2 is rejected and accepted numeric values total 6.

lessons.title: Arrow interoperability and categorical meaning
lessons.outcome: Move a typed table across an Arrow boundary while preserving its logical contract.
lessons.lab: Round-trip a table with a null through Arrow and confirm values and validity, then cast statuses to an ordered Enum and observe the rejection of an unknown category.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Values and schema round-trip; the Arrow value column has one null. Worked case 2: Business order is new, paid, shipped; unknown is rejected.

lessons.title: Nested data, lists and structs
lessons.outcome: Normalize nested events with an explicit population and identity contract.
lessons.lab: Count list lengths before exploding so empty and unknown item lists are excluded deliberately, then pack and unpack a struct and transform list elements with list.eval.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: The item table contains two rows for order 1; orders 2 and 3 remain outside that item population. Worked case 2: The struct round trip equals its source; doubled lists are [[2, 4],[6]].

lessons.title: As-of joins and knowledge available at prediction time
lessons.outcome: Reconstruct features using only information eligible at each prediction time.
lessons.lab: Match requests to features with backward and forward join_asof, then rebuild point-in-time features that require both event time and known time to precede each cutoff.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Backward values are [10, 20, 30]; forward values are [20, 30, null]. Worked case 2: Available values are [10, 30]; the leaking event-only result is [999, 30].

lessons.title: Streaming execution and bounded output
lessons.outcome: Evaluate a query under an explicit engine and resource contract.
lessons.lab: Collect the same Parquet-backed aggregate with the in-memory and streaming engines, sink it to Parquet and compare, and contrast a row-wise map with a whole-input reduction.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Both engines and the artifact readback return the same five group totals. Worked case 2: The map has 20 rows, the reduction 1 row; sum is 190 and doubled sum is 380.

lessons.title: Native expressions and the boundary of Python UDFs
lessons.outcome: Use a Python UDF only with an explicit value, type and batching contract.
lessons.lab: Show that a native square expression and a map_elements UDF agree on the fixture, then demonstrate how centering separate batches gives different values from centering the whole input.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Both implementations return [1, 4, 9]. Worked case 2: Global values are [-3, -2, -1, 6]; batch-centered values are [-0.5, 0.5, -3.5, 3.5].

lessons.title: Performance measurements with correctness controls
lessons.outcome: Produce a reviewable performance comparison with a correctness oracle.
lessons.lab: Time five collects of a lazy query while asserting each answer against an independent Python calculation, and separate sequence equality from content equality after a shuffle.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: All five results match the exact sum; timings are nonnegative and the median is reported without a speed claim. Worked case 2: The sorted values are [1, 2, 3]; bag equality holds after sorting.

lessons.title: A validated event-to-feature publication
lessons.outcome: Publish a feature artifact with explicit derivation and consumption contracts.
lessons.lab: Account for every raw event through quarantine and deduplication before aggregating per customer, then publish a Parquet feature file with a SHA-256 receipt and verify its readback.
lessons.verification: Run the starter and compare both printed results with the guide. Worked case 1: Customer 10 has total 12 from 2 events; customer 20 has total 9 from 1 event; one malformed and one duplicate row are recorded. Worked case 2: Readback preserves two unique customers, the schema and exact artifact hash.
